lessons.title: At the Airport
lessons.learn_line: Meet Mita and Zara as they wait at the airport for their first trip abroad to Thailand.
warmup: Have you ever been to an airport? What did you see there?
What do people do while waiting for a flight?
Why do travellers have to fill in forms at the airport?
How would you feel before your first ever plane journey?

reading.summary_en: Zara lives with her parents in London and has come to Bangladesh to visit her aunt and uncle. She is very close to her cousin Mita, and both families have enjoyed visiting many interesting places together. They then decide to visit Thailand, but as Mita's parents are too busy with work, Mita travels with Zara and her parents instead. Now Mita, Zara and Zara's parents are at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, waiting in the lounge to fly by Bangladesh Biman. Mita is very excited because it is her first time travelling on a plane. While they wait, the two cousins plan what they will do in Bangkok. Mita's uncle brings immigration forms for everyone to fill in, explaining that the immigration officer will check their passports and stamp them before they can travel.
reading.gist_bn: জারা তার বাবা-মায়ের সঙ্গে লন্ডনে থাকে এবং খালা-মামাকে দেখতে বাংলাদেশে এসেছে। তার চাচাতো বোন মিতার সঙ্গে সে খুব ঘনিষ্ঠ। তারা থাইল্যান্ড বেড়াতে যাওয়ার সিদ্ধান্ত নেয়, কিন্তু মিতার বাবা-মা ব্যস্ত থাকায় মিতা জারার পরিবারের সঙ্গে যায়। তারা এখন হযরত শাহজালাল আন্তর্জাতিক বিমানবন্দরের লাউঞ্জে বিমান বাংলাদেশে ওড়ার অপেক্ষায়। এটি মিতার প্রথম বিমানযাত্রা, তাই সে খুব উত্তেজিত। মামা ইমিগ্রেশন ফরম এনে দেন; ইমিগ্রেশন অফিসার পাসপোর্ট দেখে সিল মেরে দেবেন।

writing.prompt: Write a short composition about your experience of travelling to another place (about 150 words).
writing.model: Last winter I travelled to my grandparents' house in the village, and it was an experience I will never forget. The night before, I packed my bag with clothes and a few gifts, too excited to sleep properly. Early in the morning, my family and I went to the bus station, which was crowded and noisy with travellers and vendors. We boarded our bus and found our seats, and soon we were on our way. As the bus left the city, the view from the window changed into wide green fields, rivers and small villages. I enjoyed the cool breeze and the passing scenery, though the long road made me a little tired. After several hours, we finally reached our destination, where my grandparents were waiting to welcome us with warm smiles. The journey taught me that travelling is not only about reaching a place, but also about enjoying everything we see along the way.

lessons.title: Filling in a Form
lessons.learn_line: How to read travel details and fill in a departure card correctly using Mita's information.
warmup: Have you ever filled in an official form? What details did it ask for?
What is a passport, and what is a visa?
What does it mean if a passport 'expires'?
Why must travel documents be 'valid'?

reading.summary_en: This lesson teaches how to fill in a departure card using Mita's travel information. Mita's full name is Mita Sultana Ahmed, and she was born on 6 May 1998. She got her passport on 9 June 2010; it is a five-year passport that will expire on 8 June 2015, after which she must renew it. Her passport number is AB 9842251. She is going to Thailand by Bangladesh Biman on flight number BG 88 on 14 July 2012. She got her visa from the Royal Thai Embassy in Dhaka; her visa number is T 9115138, and it was issued in Dhaka on 29 June 2012. The visa is valid for three months and will expire on 27 September 2012. It is a tourist visa, which means she is not allowed to study or work there. Reading such details carefully helps a traveller complete forms accurately.
reading.gist_bn: এই পাঠে মিতার তথ্য দিয়ে ডিপারচার কার্ড পূরণ করা শেখানো হয়। মিতার পুরো নাম মিতা সুলতানা আহমেদ, জন্ম ৬ মে ১৯৯৮। সে ৯ জুন ২০১০-এ পাসপোর্ট পায়; এটি পাঁচ বছরের, মেয়াদ শেষ হবে ৮ জুন ২০১৫, এরপর নবায়ন (renew) করতে হবে। পাসপোর্ট নম্বর AB 9842251। সে ১৪ জুলাই ২০১২-এ বিমান বাংলাদেশের BG 88 ফ্লাইটে থাইল্যান্ড যাচ্ছে। ভিসা পেয়েছে ঢাকার রয়্যাল থাই দূতাবাস থেকে; ভিসা নম্বর T 9115138, ইস্যু ২৯ জুন ২০১২, তিন মাস বৈধ, মেয়াদ শেষ ২৭ সেপ্টেম্বর ২০১২। এটি ট্যুরিস্ট ভিসা—পড়াশোনা বা কাজ করা যাবে না।

writing.prompt: Write a short paragraph on 'The Importance of a Passport and Visa' (about 80 words).
writing.model: A passport and a visa are essential documents for anyone travelling abroad. A passport is an official identity document, issued by one's own country, that proves who a traveller is and allows them to travel internationally. A visa, on the other hand, is the permission given by the country one wishes to visit. Both must be valid and not expired; once a passport expires, it has to be renewed. Different visas, such as tourist, student or work visas, allow different activities. Carrying valid travel documents lets us cross borders safely and legally.

lessons.title: Going Through Immigration
lessons.learn_line: What happens at an immigration counter, through Mita's conversation with the officer.
warmup: Why does a person need a passport to travel abroad?
What do the small booths at immigration counters do?
Why do travellers stand in lines at immigration?
What questions might an immigration officer ask you?

reading.summary_en: In this dialogue, Zara's parents, Mrs Jhuma Islam and Mr Mazharul Islam, Zara and Mita fill in their departure cards and move towards the immigration counter. Mita stands in front of one of the booths and hands her passport and departure card to the officer. The officer goes through her passport, visa and departure card and asks if she is travelling alone; Mita replies that she is going with her aunt, uncle and cousin, who are at the next counter. The officer also asks if it is her first visit to Thailand (yes), how long she will stay (seven to ten days) and where she will stay (in a hotel). Finding her papers in order, the officer smiles, stamps her passport, keeps the departure card and returns the passport, wishing her a safe journey. Mita waits on the other side until the whole family is done, and they all walk towards the passengers' departure lounge.
reading.gist_bn: এই কথোপকথনে জারার বাবা-মা (মিসেস ঝুমা ইসলাম ও মি. মাজহারুল ইসলাম), জারা ও মিতা ডিপারচার কার্ড পূরণ করে ইমিগ্রেশন কাউন্টারের দিকে যায়। মিতা একটি বুথের সামনে দাঁড়িয়ে পাসপোর্ট ও কার্ড অফিসারকে দেয়। অফিসার পাসপোর্ট, ভিসা ও কার্ড দেখে জিজ্ঞেস করেন—একা যাচ্ছ? (না, খালা-মামা-কাজিনসহ), এটাই কি প্রথম থাইল্যান্ড সফর? (হ্যাঁ), কতদিন থাকবে? (৭-১০ দিন), কোথায় থাকবে? (হোটেলে)। কাগজপত্র ঠিক থাকায় অফিসার হেসে পাসপোর্টে সিল মেরে ফেরত দেন এবং নিরাপদ যাত্রা কামনা করেন।

writing.prompt: Make a dialogue between an immigration officer and a traveller going abroad for the first time.
writing.model:
Officer: Good morning. May I see your passport and departure card, please?
Traveller: Good morning, officer. Here they are.
Officer: Thank you. Are you travelling alone?
Traveller: Yes, I am travelling alone this time.
Officer: Is this your first visit to Malaysia?
Traveller: Yes, it is my very first trip abroad.
Officer: I see. What is the purpose of your visit?
Traveller: I am going there as a tourist to visit a few famous places.
Officer: How long do you plan to stay?
Traveller: About one week, sir.
Officer: And where will you be staying?
Traveller: In a hotel near the city centre.
Officer: Everything looks fine. I am stamping your passport now. Have a safe journey.
Traveller: Thank you very much, officer.

lessons.learn_line: Airport security rules about hand luggage and liquids, as the family boards the plane.
warmup: What things are you not allowed to carry in your hand luggage on a plane?

reading.summary_en: Mita, Zara, Mr and Mrs Islam sit at the lounge with their hand luggage. Mr Islam asks Mita and Zara whether they are carrying any liquid, lotion, gel or cream in their carry-on luggage. Mita has a small lip gel, and her uncle explains that a very small one is no problem, but anything more than 100 ml must be put in the checked-in luggage, because such items are not allowed in hand luggage. For security reasons, the officials who do the baggage checking will seize and throw such items away. The family goes through the security checking and waits in the enclosed area until all the formalities are done. When their row number is announced, they board the plane: Mita gets a window seat, number F23C, Zara sits beside her on an aisle seat, and her parents sit behind them.

writing.model: Airport security rules are made to keep all passengers safe during a flight. Before boarding, every traveller and their bags must pass through a security check. lessons.title: Announcements on Board (1)
lessons.learn_line: The pre-take-off and the captain's announcements that passengers hear on a flight.
warmup: What kinds of announcements do you hear on a plane?

reading.summary_en: This lesson presents the announcements heard on board Flight BG 88 to Bangkok. In the pre-take-off announcement, passengers are welcomed and told the plane is third in line for take-off and expected to be in the air in about seven minutes. They are asked to fasten their seat belts, secure their baggage under the seat or in the overhead compartments, keep their seats and table trays upright, and turn off all personal electronic devices including laptops and cellphones. It is a non-smoking flight, and smoking in the lavatory is prohibited. Later, the captain, Rashid Akbar, welcomes everyone and announces that the plane is cruising at an altitude of about 10,058 feet at an airspeed of about 643 km per hour, that the time is 1:25 pm, and that with a tailwind they expect to land in Bangkok about fifteen minutes ahead of schedule. The weather in Bangkok is clear and sunny at 32 degrees Celsius, the cabin crew will soon serve snacks and drinks, and an inflight movie will follow.

lessons.title: Announcements on Board (2)
lessons.learn_line: The safety announcement: oxygen masks, the bracing position and the life vest.
warmup: Why do cabin crew explain safety rules before a flight?
What should you do if an oxygen mask drops down?
Where is a life vest kept on a plane?
What is turbulence, and how should passengers behave during it?

reading.summary_en: This lesson is the safety announcement made on board. It explains that oxygen and air pressure are always monitored, and that if there is a lack of oxygen, an oxygen mask will automatically appear; passengers should pull it towards them, place it firmly over the nose and mouth, secure the elastic band behind the head and breathe normally. If travelling with a child or someone who needs assistance, one should secure one's own mask first and then help the other person. In an emergency, passengers should assume the bracing position by leaning forward with hands on top of the head and elbows against the thighs, keeping the feet flat on the floor. A life vest is located in a pouch under the seat or between the armrests; when instructed, passengers should open the pouch, slip the vest over the head, pass the straps around the waist, and inflate it by pulling the red cord, but only before leaving the aircraft. It is a non-smoking flight, and all safety information is given in the card in the seat pocket. The cabin crew's kind behaviour made the passengers feel safe and happy, even during turbulence when the plane was bumping.
reading.gist_bn: এই পাঠ হলো প্লেনে দেওয়া নিরাপত্তা ঘোষণা। অক্সিজেন ও বায়ুচাপ সবসময় পর্যবেক্ষণ করা হয়; অক্সিজেন কমে গেলে মাস্ক স্বয়ংক্রিয়ভাবে নেমে আসবে—টেনে নাক-মুখে চেপে ধরে ইলাস্টিক মাথার পেছনে আটকে স্বাভাবিকভাবে শ্বাস নিতে হবে। শিশু বা সহায়তা-প্রয়োজন কারো সঙ্গে থাকলে আগে নিজের মাস্ক পরে তারপর তাকে সাহায্য করতে হবে। জরুরি অবস্থায় ব্রেসিং পজিশন নিতে হবে। সিটের নিচে পাউচে লাইফ-ভেস্ট থাকে—মাথা গলিয়ে, কোমরে স্ট্র্যাপ বেঁধে, লাল কর্ড টেনে ফোলাতে হবে (প্লেন থেকে নামার আগে)। ক্রুদের ভালো ব্যবহারে ঝাঁকুনির (turbulence) সময়ও যাত্রীরা নিরাপদ বোধ করেন।

lessons.title: Reaching Bangkok
lessons.learn_line: Facts about Bangkok's huge Suvarnabhumi Airport, where Mita's flight finally lands.
warmup: What is the name of the biggest airport you know?
What facilities does a large international airport have?
Why might an airport need several runways?
What does the word 'capacity' mean?

reading.summary_en: The plane lands at Suvarnabhumi Airport at 4:55 p.m. The name 'Suvarnabhumi' is pronounced 'su-wan-na-poom' and is derived from Sanskrit, meaning 'golden land'; it was chosen by the late King Bhumibol Adulyadej. The airport is located in Racha Thewa subdistrict in the Bang Phli district of Samut Prakan province, 30 kilometres east of Bangkok. It has three parallel runways, all 60 metres wide; two are 4,000 metres long and the other is 3,700 metres. It can handle 94 flight operations per hour, 45 million passengers and 3 million tonnes of cargo per year. The airport has two terminals, a main terminal and a satellite terminal; the main terminal is 563,000 square metres, that is, 6,060,000 square feet, and is the fourth largest passenger terminal building in the world. The airport is going through phase 2, which will raise its capacity to handle 65 million passengers per year, and it has two five-storey car park buildings that can house 5,000 cars.

writing.prompt: Write a short paragraph describing 'An International Airport' (about 100 words).
writing.model: An international airport is a huge and busy place that connects a country with the rest of the world. It has long parallel runways where giant planes take off and land throughout the day and night. Inside the large terminal buildings, passengers check in their luggage, pass through immigration and security, and wait in comfortable lounges before boarding. Big airports like Suvarnabhumi in Bangkok can handle millions of passengers and millions of tonnes of cargo every year. They also have shops, restaurants, car parks and satellite terminals. lessons.title: The Destination
lessons.learn_line: Mita's taxi ride to the apartment and a visit to the traditional Tha Kha floating market.
warmup: How do travellers get from an airport to their hotel?
What is a 'floating market'? Have you seen one?
What would you like to buy at a market on boats?
Why might local people at a small market all know each other?

reading.summary_en: Mita is fascinated to see such a big airport. After immigration, Mr Mazharul Islam buys a taxi ticket, and the family takes a taxi to their apartment at Happy Condo, 18 Rachada Pisek Road. The ride takes about one and a half hours, and Mita, very excited, holds Zara's hand, saying she can't believe she is there and that she has never ridden in a car at such high speed, though she is a little scared. At the apartment, Mita loves the garden of trees and flowers with a small fountain bringing a cool breeze. They take the elevator to the seventh floor and stay in a nicely done two-bedroom apartment, where Mita and Zara share a room. After dinner, they plan the next day: Mita has read about a floating market and wants to see one, so Mr Islam decides to take them to the Tha Kha floating market, which sits early in the morning and is over before noon. At the market, sellers and buyers row their boats slowly, displaying and choosing fruits, vegetables, local food and delicious sweets, chatting as they trade. The Tha Kha floating market is more traditional, with fewer tourists; it used to sit only six or seven days a month depending on the phase of the moon, but now trades on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays too. The main buyers are local Tha Kha people who know each other very well, smiling and calling each other by name, so busy buying and selling that they hardly notice Mita and the others.

writing.prompt: Write a paragraph on 'A Visit to a Market' (about 100 words).
writing.model: Last week I visited a busy local market with my father, and it was a lively experience. As soon as we entered, we saw rows of shops and stalls selling fresh fruits, vegetables, fish, sweets and many other things. The sellers called out the prices of their goods, while buyers bargained cheerfully before making their choices. The air was full of colours, sounds and the smell of fresh food. I especially enjoyed watching the fruit sellers arrange their bright oranges and bananas. Although the market was crowded and noisy, everyone seemed friendly and happy. The visit showed me how a market brings people together in daily life.
